nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Ziziphus : From the ancient Greek name zizufon for Zizyphus jujuba, from the Arabic zizouf or zizafun.
- Jujuba : From the Arabic name jujube.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Ziziphus jujuba is dark greyish-coloured with vertical furrows. Ziziphus jujuba is armed with recurved stipular thorns.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Ziziphus jujuba is dark greyish-coloured with vertical furrows. Ziziphus jujuba is armed with recurved stipular thorns.

seed.text: The seed of Ziziphus jujuba is enclosed into a globose en rough stone. The stone is 1-1.5 cm across and contains one seed.
seed.text_html: The seed of Ziziphus jujuba is enclosed into a globose en rough stone. The stone is 1-1.5 cm across and contains one seed.

fruit.text: The fruit of Ziziphus jujuba is a subglobose drupe . It is 2-2.5 cm across, green turning brown-reddish when ripe with a 4-5 mm long peduncle. Each fruit contains one stone.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Ziziphus jujuba is a subglobose drupe. It is 2-2.5 cm across, green turning brown-reddish when ripe with a 4-5 mm long peduncle. Each fruit contains one stone.

leaf.text: The leaves of Ziziphus jujuba grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The shape of the leaves are very variable. The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is glossy, chartaceous and glabrous above. The leaves have a 6-8 mm long petiole . The leaf of Ziziphus jujuba is 5-10 cm long and 3-5 cm wide. The shape of the blade is elliptic, the apex is acute or obtuse, the base is rounded and the margins are denticulate. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with 3 prominent veins.
leaf.text_html:
The leaves of Ziziphus jujuba grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged).
The shape of the leaves are very variable.
The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is glossy, chartaceous and glabrous above.
The leaves have a 6-8 mm long petiole.
The leaf of Ziziphus jujuba is 5-10 cm long and 3-5 cm wide. The shape of the blade is elliptic, the apex is acute or obtuse, the base is rounded and the margins are denticulate.
The venation of the leaf is reticulate with 3 prominent veins.

habit.text: Ziziphus jujuba is a thorny, small-sized and deciduous tree growing up to 10-12 m high.
habit.text_html: Ziziphus jujuba is a thorny, small-sized and deciduous tree growing up to 10-12 m high.

distribution.text: The precise natural distribution of Ziziphus jujuba is uncertain due to extensive cultivation, but is thought to be in southern Asia (between Lebanon, northern India, and southern and central China).
distribution.text_html:
• Distribution :

    The precise natural distribution of Ziziphus jujuba is uncertain due to extensive cultivation, but is thought to be in southern Asia (between Lebanon, northern India, and southern and central China).

reproduction_dispersal.text: Ziziphus jujuba is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Ziziphus jujuba is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Ziziphus jujuba are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Ziziphus jujuba is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Ziziphus jujuba is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Ziziphus jujuba are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

veterinary.text: The leaves of Ziziphus jujuba are used as fodder for goats and sheep.

handicrafts.text: The wood of Ziziphus jujuba is hard, durable, close-grained and takes a good polish. It is used for agricultural implements, well construction, tool handles, turnery... The bark is used as a tanning material. Sources : - Dastur, 2006, Useful Plants of India and Pakistan - Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide

medicinal.text: Ziziphus jujuba is used in Ayurveda, Unani and Siddha medicines. The bark is astringent, constipating and tonic, and is useful in dysentery, diarrhoea, gingivitis and boils. The stem bark decoction is used to check diarrhea. The leaves are febrifuge. The leaves paste are applied on the affected portion to cure scorpion sting. The fruit is astringent, anodyne, cooling, expectorant and stomachic. Sources : - Arya Vaidya Sala, 1996, Indian Medicinal plants - Basu & Kirtikar, 1918, Indian Medicinal Plants - Chopra, 1956, Glossary of Indian medicinal plants - Khare, 2007, Indian Medicinal Plants, An Illustrated Dictionary - Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide - Quattrocchi, 2012, CRC World Dictionary of Medicinal and Poisonous Plants
medicinal.text_html:
Ziziphus jujuba is used in Ayurveda, Unani and Siddha medicines.

The bark is astringent, constipating and tonic, and is useful in dysentery, diarrhoea, gingivitis and boils.
The stem bark decoction is used to check diarrhea.

The leaves are febrifuge.
The leaves paste are applied on the affected portion to cure scorpion sting.

The fruit is astringent, anodyne, cooling, expectorant and stomachic.

Sources :
- Arya Vaidya Sala, 1996, Indian Medicinal plants
- Basu & Kirtikar, 1918, Indian Medicinal Plants
- Chopra, 1956, Glossary of Indian medicinal plants

reforestation.text: Ziziphus jujuba is a light demander and fairly drought resistant. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining. The species is propagated by seeds or by cuttings. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Ziziphus jujuba is a light demander and fairly drought resistant. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining.
    The species is propagated by seeds or by cuttings.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
